sql: SELECT COALESCE(SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price), 0) - COALESCE(SUM(r.refund_amount), 0) AS net_revenue FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id LEFT JOIN refunds r ON o.order_id = r.order_id WHERE o.status != 'cancelled' AND o.ordered_at >= '2026-08-01 00:00:00' AND o.ordered_at < '2026-09-01 00:00:00'
assumptions: Net revenue is calculated as total gross sales from non-cancelled order items minus total refunds for orders in August 2026.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(sub.order_total), 2) AS average_order_value FROM (SELECT o.order_id, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) - COALESCE(o.discount_amount, 0) AS order_total FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status != 'cancelled' GROUP BY o.order_id, o.discount_amount) sub
assumptions: Order value is calculated as the sum of order items (quantity * unit_price) minus discount amount for non-cancelled orders.

refusal_reason: The database does not contain a definition or tracking mechanism for 'active' customers (e.g. definition of what makes a customer active within a time window).

sql: SELECT count(*) AS new_customers FROM customers WHERE signup_at >= TIMESTAMP '2026-07-01 00:00:00' AND signup_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-08-01 00:00:00'
assumptions: New customers are defined as those who signed up in July 2026.

sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'cancelled' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)::DOUBLE / COUNT(*), 4) AS cancellation_rate FROM orders WHERE ordered_at >= date_trunc('year', CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)
assumptions: Cancellation rate is defined as the number of cancelled orders divided by the total number of orders.
This year so far is defined as orders with ordered_at from the start of the current calendar year up to the current timestamp.

sql: SELECT SUM(quantity * unit_price) AS gmv FROM order_items JOIN orders ON order_items.order_id = orders.order_id WHERE orders.ordered_at >= date_trunc('month', current_date - interval '1 month') AND orders.ordered_at < date_trunc('month', current_date)
assumptions: GMV is defined as the total value of items ordered (quantity * unit_price) before discounts and refunds.
Last month refers to the calendar month prior to the current system date.

sql: SELECT COUNT(order_id) AS order_count FROM orders WHERE ordered_at >= TIMESTAMP '2026-08-15 00:00:00' AND ordered_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-08-16 00:00:00'
assumptions: Dates refer to the UTC timezone as stored in ordered_at.

sql: SELECT COUNT(order_id) AS pending_orders_count FROM orders WHERE status = 'pending'
assumptions: Pending orders are identified where the status column equals 'pending'.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS repeat_customers FROM (SELECT customer_id FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(order_id) > 1) t
assumptions: A repeat customer is defined as a customer who has placed more than one order.

sql: SELECT o.customer_id AS customer_id, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS lifetime_value FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status != 'cancelled' GROUP BY o.customer_id ORDER BY lifetime_value DESC LIMIT 5
assumptions: Lifetime value is calculated as the sum of quantity multiplied by unit_price for all non-cancelled orders associated with a customer.

sql: SELECT COALESCE(SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price), 0) - COALESCE(SUM(o.discount_amount), 0) - COALESCE(SUM(r.refund_amount), 0) AS net_revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id LEFT JOIN refunds r ON o.order_id = r.order_id WHERE o.ordered_at >= NOW() - INTERVAL '7 days'
assumptions: Net revenue is defined as total item sales (quantity * unit_price) minus discounts and refunds over the last 7 days based on the order timestamp.

refusal_reason: The database contains refunds, but return rate could be defined either by order count or item count, and the specific definition of return rate is not provided.

sql: SELECT c.city AS city, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) - COALESCE(SUM(r.refund_amount), 0) AS net_revenue FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id LEFT JOIN refunds r ON o.order_id = r.order_id WHERE o.status != 'cancelled' GROUP BY c.city ORDER BY net_revenue DESC LIMIT 1
assumptions: Net revenue is defined as total order item sales (quantity * unit_price) minus refunds for non-cancelled orders.
If multiple cities tied for the highest net revenue, a limit of 1 returns one of them.

sql: SELECT c.acquisition_channel AS channel, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS gmv FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status != 'cancelled' GROUP BY c.acquisition_channel
assumptions: GMV is calculated as the sum of quantity * unit_price for all order items associated with non-cancelled orders.
Customers with null acquisition_channel will be grouped as such.

sql: SELECT t1.category, SUM(t1.quantity * t1.unit_price) AS gmv FROM order_items AS t1 JOIN orders AS t2 ON t1.order_id = t2.order_id WHERE t2.ordered_at >= TIMESTAMP '2026-07-01 00:00:00' AND t2.ordered_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-08-01 00:00:00' AND t2.status != 'cancelled' GROUP BY t1.category
assumptions: GMV is calculated as quantity multiplied by unit_price for all non-cancelled orders in the specified month.

sql: SELECT date_trunc('month', signup_at)::date AS month_date, COUNT(customer_id) AS new_customers FROM customers WHERE signup_at >= TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00' AND signup_at < TIMESTAMP '2027-01-01 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
assumptions: New customers are defined as customers whose signup_at timestamp falls within the specified year 2026.

sql: SELECT count(*) AS customer_count FROM customers AS c WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders AS o WHERE o.customer_id = c.customer_id AND o.status = 'completed')

sql: SELECT SUM(r.refund_amount) AS total_refunded_amount FROM refunds r JOIN orders o ON r.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed'
assumptions: Completed orders are identified by status = 'completed' in the orders table.

sql: SELECT c.city, COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_id) AS repeat_customers FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.city HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) > 1 ORDER BY repeat_customers DESC LIMIT 3
assumptions: A repeat customer is defined as a customer who has placed more than one order.
